section: India - literacy: levels, gender and regional gaps, trends

accepted.s: According to the Census definition, a literate person is one who:
o: is aged seven years or above and can both read and write with understanding in any language
is aged five years or above and can read and write without understanding
is aged ten years or above and has completed primary education
is aged seven years or above and can only read in any language
accepted.x: A literate person is aged seven years or above and must be able to both read and write with understanding in any language. A person who can only read is not treated as literate.
accepted.tq: Use the exact official definition and distinguish ‘read and write with understanding’ from merely reading.
accepted.sec: Literacy Census 2011 - definition of literate (age threshold), national rate, male vs female  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The age threshold of seven years for measuring literacy in the Indian Census was introduced from:
accepted.x: Censuses from 1951 to 1971 counted literacy for persons aged five years and above. The seven-years-and-above threshold was adopted from 1981.
accepted.tq: For close historical figures, identify the year marking the change rather than the years preceding it.
accepted.sec: Literacy Census 2011 - definition of literate (age threshold), national rate, male vs female  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the provisional Census 2011 literacy figures, consider the following statements:
1. Male literacy was 82.14%.
2. Female literacy was 65.46%.
3. The total literacy rate was 73.0%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The provisional figures were 82.14% for males and 65.46% for females. The total provisional figure was 74.04%, whereas 73.0% refers to the final figure.
accepted.tq: Separate provisional and final values before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Literacy Census 2011 - definition of literate (age threshold), national rate, male vs female  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The final Census 2011 literacy rate of India, as cited in the India Year Book, was approximately:
accepted.x: The final Census 2011 literacy rate was 73.0%, or 72.98% when expressed more precisely.
accepted.tq: Choose the rounded final value rather than the provisional or survey-based figures.
accepted.sec: Literacy Census 2011 - definition of literate (age threshold), national rate, male vs female  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The literacy rate of India in 2001 was approximately:
accepted.x: India’s literacy rate in 2001 was 64.8% according to the cited India Year Book figure.
accepted.tq: Match the decade with its corresponding national literacy percentage.
accepted.sec: Literacy Census 2011 - definition of literate (age threshold), national rate, male vs female  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 1951, the proportion of women who were literate in India was:
accepted.x: Female literacy in 1951 was 8.9%, meaning that fewer than one in ten women were literate.
accepted.tq: Convert the percentage into the comparative expression used in the question.
accepted.sec: Literacy Census 2011 - definition of literate (age threshold), national rate, male vs female  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State had the highest literacy rate in Census 2011 according to the final figures cited?
accepted.x: Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among the States, at 94.0%. Mizoram was also highly placed but lower at 91.3%.
accepted.tq: Identify the leading State from a ranking table and reject the nearby high-ranking distractors.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bihar — 94.0% total literacy and 92.1% female literacy
Kerala — 94.0% total literacy and 92.1% female literacy
accepted.x: Kerala recorded 94.0% total literacy and 92.1% female literacy. Bihar had the lowest total literacy at 61.8% and female literacy at 51.5%.
accepted.tq: Check both components of each pair; APPSC commonly swaps values between high- and low-ranking units.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following had the lowest total literacy rate among the States in Census 2011?
accepted.x: Bihar had the lowest total literacy rate among the States, at 61.8%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the lowest State in the Census ranking from later survey-based rankings.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Lakshadweep occupied which position in the Census 2011 literacy ranking mentioned in the material?
accepted.x: Lakshadweep was second, with a literacy rate of 91.8%, after Kerala’s 94.0%.
accepted.tq: Use the ranking and the exact percentage together to discriminate between close alternatives.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State had the largest gender gap in literacy in 2011?
accepted.x: Rajasthan had the largest gender gap in literacy, at 28 percentage points. The national gender gap was 16 percentage points.
accepted.tq: Do not confuse the State with the lowest female literacy with the State having the largest gender gap.
accepted.sec: Gender gap in literacy - largest-gap states  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The national gender gap in literacy in 2011 was approximately:
accepted.x: The national gender gap in literacy in 2011 was about 16 percentage points. Rajasthan recorded the larger State-level gap of 28 points.
accepted.tq: Separate the national figure from the maximum State-level figure.
accepted.sec: Gender gap in literacy - largest-gap states  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the final Census 2011 female literacy ranking fact?
o: Andhra Pradesh had the highest female literacy at 92.1%.
Kerala had the highest female literacy at 92.1%.
Rajasthan had the highest female literacy at 92.1%.
Bihar had the highest female literacy at 92.1%.
accepted.x: Kerala had the highest female literacy rate, at 92.1%. Bihar had the lowest female literacy rate, at 51.5%.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the highest and lowest female-literacy States using the same numerical pair.
accepted.sec: Gender gap in literacy - largest-gap states  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a cause of the gender gap in literacy?
o: High concentration of specialised universities in cities
Distance to schools and safety concerns
accepted.x: The cited causes include distance to schools and safety, early marriage, dowry, son preference and poverty. Concentration of specialised universities in cities is not listed as a cause.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated addition among a cluster of recognised social causes.
accepted.sec: Gender gap in literacy - largest-gap states  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to Census 2011 provisional figures, the rural and urban literacy rates of India were respectively:
accepted.x: The Census 2011 provisional rural literacy rate was 68.9%, while the urban rate was 85.0%.
accepted.tq: Match the pair to the correct data source and distinguish Census figures from PLFS figures.
accepted.sec: Rural-urban literacy differential

accepted.s: Under PLFS 2023-24, the urban-rural literacy figures for India were approximately:
accepted.x: PLFS 2023-24 reported urban literacy of 88.9% and rural literacy of 77.5%, leaving a gap of about 11 percentage points.
accepted.tq: Keep the urban-rural order fixed and distinguish it from the male-female pair.
accepted.sec: Rural-urban literacy differential

accepted.s: Which section of the population faces the largest literacy deficit in the rural-urban context?
accepted.x: Rural women face the largest literacy deficit. Rural areas also have lower literacy overall than urban areas.
accepted.tq: Apply the combined rural disadvantage and gender disadvantage to identify the most vulnerable group.
accepted.sec: Rural-urban literacy differential

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Census years in ascending order of India’s literacy rate:
A. 1951
B. 1981
C. 1961
D. 2001
accepted.x: The literacy rates rose from 18.33% in 1951 to 28.30% in 1961, 43.57% in 1981 and 64.83% in 2001. Therefore, the order is A, C, B, D.
accepted.tq: Arrange the years by the steadily increasing literacy percentages, not merely by visual year spacing.
accepted.sec: Trends since 1951 - decadal improvement

accepted.s: Which Census year recorded the largest decadal improvement in India’s literacy rate?
accepted.x: The largest decadal gain came in the 1990s, culminating in the 1991 Census period. Growth slowed during 2001–2011.
accepted.tq: Compare successive Census increments rather than selecting the latest year automatically.
accepted.sec: Trends since 1951 - decadal improvement

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India’s literacy trend:
1. Literacy increased from 18.33% in 1951 to 74.04% in 2011.
2. Male literacy rose from about 27% to about 82% over the sixty-year period.
3. The largest decadal gain occurred during 2001–2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the largest decadal gain occurred in the 1990s, while growth slowed in 2001–2011.
accepted.tq: Identify the false trend statement by testing the claimed decade against the stated growth pattern.
accepted.sec: Trends since 1951 - decadal improvement

accepted.s: The literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh increased from 62.07% in 2001 to which figure in 2011?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s total literacy rate increased from 62.07% in 2001 to 67.35% in 2011.
accepted.tq: Match the State, Census year and total figure while rejecting male, female and national values.
accepted.sec: Trends since 1951 - decadal improvement

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly gives the literacy trend of Andhra Pradesh from 1981 to 2011?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh sequence was 29.94% in 1981, 45.86% in 1991, 62.07% in 2001 and 67.35% in 2011.
accepted.tq: Use a complete State-specific sequence and reject options that substitute national or gender figures.
accepted.sec: Trends since 1951 - decadal improvement

accepted.s: The total literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011 was:
o: higher than the national average by more than five points
higher than the national average by more than ten points
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 67.35% literacy in Census 2011, below India’s national figure of about 72.98%.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of the comparison before considering the numerical values.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the NSS 75th round for July 2017–June 2018, which State was placed lowest among the States in literacy?
accepted.x: The NSS 75th round placed Andhra Pradesh lowest among the States. Its female literacy was approximately 59.5%; Rajasthan, not Uttar Pradesh, had the lowest female literacy in the cited comparison.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State with the lowest overall literacy from the State with the lowest female literacy.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under PLFS 2023-24, India’s literacy rate for persons aged seven years and above was:
accepted.x: PLFS 2023-24 reported an overall literacy rate of 80.9% for persons aged seven years and above. The urban rate was 88.9%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the overall survey rate from its urban component and from Census figures.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the PLFS 2023-24 male-female literacy figures for India?
accepted.x: PLFS 2023-24 recorded male literacy of 87.2% and female literacy of 74.6%. Their difference was about 12.6 percentage points.
accepted.tq: Separate the male-female pair from the overall and urban-rural pairs in the same survey.
accepted.sec: Gender gap in literacy - largest-gap states

accepted.s: Which of the following was the PLFS-based literacy ranking pattern cited for 2023-24?
o: Top: Kerala, Goa, Mizoram; bottom: Bihar, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh
Top: Mizoram, Lakshadweep, Nagaland; bottom: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh
Top: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh; bottom: Mizoram, Lakshadweep, Nagaland
Top: Kerala, Lakshadweep, Bihar; bottom: Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Goa
accepted.x: The PLFS-based top units were Mizoram, Lakshadweep and Nagaland, while Andhra Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh were at the bottom of the cited grouping.
accepted.tq: Match the complete top-bottom grouping rather than relying on one familiar high-literacy State.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh under the specified source?
accepted.x: The AP literacy rate was 69.10% in PLFS 2018-19, 72.60% in PLFS 2023-24 and 71.40% for calendar year 2025 as cited. The Census 2011 figure was 67.35%.
accepted.tq: Match each percentage with its source and year; official figures are often swapped across surveys.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The claim that Andhra Pradesh had a literacy rate of 82.10% in 2026 was disputed primarily because:
o: no official estimate for 2026 was available
the Census had already recorded a lower final figure in 2011
the figure referred only to male literacy
accepted.x: The 82.10% claim was disputed because no official 2026 estimate existed. The cited calendar-year 2025 figure was 71.40%.
accepted.tq: Test whether a current numerical claim is supported by an officially available estimate.
accepted.sec: State ranking - highest/lowest literacy states and UTs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the literacy rates of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in 2011?
accepted.x: The cited 2011 literacy rate was 66.1% for Scheduled Castes and 59.0% for Scheduled Tribes. Both were below the national literacy level of about 73–74%.
accepted.tq: Keep the social-category labels attached to the correct percentages and avoid confusing national and State figures.
accepted.sec: Literacy among SC/ST populations

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Pradesh ST literacy — 48.8%; Telangana ST literacy — 49.5%
Andhra Pradesh ST literacy — 59.0%; Telangana ST literacy — 66.1%
Andhra Pradesh SC literacy — 48.8%; Telangana SC literacy — 49.5%
Andhra Pradesh ST literacy — 73.0%; Telangana ST literacy — 74.6%
accepted.x: The cited figures were 48.8% for Scheduled Tribe literacy in Andhra Pradesh and 49.5% in Telangana.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure State-category pair and reject options that substitute national or SC values.
accepted.sec: Literacy among SC/ST populations

accepted.s: Low literacy is recognised as one of the four criteria for identifying:
accepted.x: Low literacy is one of the four criteria used in relation to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).
accepted.tq: Link the social indicator to the exact administrative category rather than a broader population group.
accepted.sec: Literacy among SC/ST populations
